lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Before this blog existed, where did Antoine put his front-end experiments? On CodePen, which he calls his public lab notebook.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So this page is a bookmark of old pens?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pretty much. It collects live embeds from the jQuery and vanilla JavaScript years, around 2016 and 2017. Small UI labs first, then two bigger demos.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A sign-up form, a terminal-style console with a blinking cursor, a sticky header with jump links, a step progress bar, a date range picker and a countdown timer that plays a sound at zero.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A screen capture demo using getDisplayMedia, with a live preview and a red recording border.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A full-screen HTML5 canvas blackboard where you pick a pen color and size, drag in images, save a PNG, or erase everything. And a Three.js wave, a grid of green cubes moving with a sine wave, which you can orbit with the mouse, keyboard or even a gamepad.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Which ones does he still reopen?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The blackboard and the wave. When someone asks whether he can prototype a UI fast, those are the pens he goes back to.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He says CodePen is where he learned feedback loops under four hundred lines.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The page links every pen, so you can fork anything. The full page has the live embeds.
